c: says something must not change: "the bathroom is final", "keep this wall nine feet long", "keep the stair hall three feet wide". Locks are not part of the document — they are a decision the person editing has made about it — so they arrive in the apply request's
, from whatever store keeps them, and they are checked after normalization against the committed result.

head: Lock
Holds while
rows: the element exists, in the same collection, with exactly its content in A; for a wall or separator, its start and end junctions are also unmoved; for a room, every junction on its face's outer cycle is also unmoved; for an extension element on a wall face, its wall's start and end junctions are also unmoved
the wall exists and its location line has the same length as in A
both walls exist, are parallel, and the distance between their location lines is as in A

c: An element lock on a program item or an extension element holds its content; on an outlet, it also holds the wall the outlet is on, since an outlet follows its wall (
) — "this outlet is final" means it does not move. Comparisons are exact: content in canonical form (constant defaults omitted, Core §

, values equal when their RFC 8785 serializations are), positions as integers, lengths by their squares, distances by squared cross products. Locks are checked only on a valid result: a result that is both invalid and breaks a lock is rejected with its Core diagnostics alone (
A lock whose elements do not exist in A, a length or distance lock that names an element that is not a wall in A, or a distance lock between walls not parallel in A, MUST be rejected with
